rows.notes: The cited study is a narrative review (labelled 'Review' in the journal header) of plant physiological and molecular responses to drought; it reports no data of its own. It does not address drip irrigation at all; irrigation is mentioned only in passing (e.g. stomatal conductance in irrigated cotton/wheat citing Lu et al. 1997, thermal imaging for irrigation scheduling, partial root-zone drying citing Stoll et al. 2000). No evidence on drip irrigation improving WUE.

Narrative review without own data. Irrigation calendars based on soil salinity and water table depth are not discussed anywhere; the only scheduling-related remark is a general statement that thermal imaging may become useful for field irrigation scheduling, which is a prospect, not a result. No evidence on scheduling-based water conservation.

notes: The study is a review article (Chaves, Maroco & Pereira 2003, Functional Plant Biology) synthesising literature on plant drought responses from genes to whole plant; it contains no primary data, experiments, surveys or validated model runs. It is misattributed support for both irrigation-technology claims; its only link to the reviewing passage is general discussion of water-use efficiency physiology and stable isotope/imaging tools.
